text_fidelity_a:
Ab Rocket Twister Abdominal Trainer, Red For about 5 years, I've been the not-so-proud owners of a much lesser piece of abdominal training equipment, the kind that cushions your head and helps you roll through crunches. It's been nice, but it hurts my neck and it doesn't do anything for your lower abs, which is probably the biggest problem I have with it, and which is the reason that I use it far less than most of my other exercise equipment.

When I saw the Ab Rocket Twister, I immediately saw this as an improvement over what I had. It is that, certainly. The main function of this machine is actually opposite of what my old machine was used for - with the ab rocket twister, you usually end up pushing down rather than up. This has the added advantage of working your lower back muscles just a little bit as you work out, though I did notice that my abs were less strained after going through the exercise video with this than with my other piece of equipment.

It's a bit of a pain to assemble, and it's garishly colored, but it's pretty good for what it does. Keep in mind when you're looking at this that you could certainly do all of the exercises without the machine, and many more, without getting it. A good crunch-and-bicycle kick will do you far better than this will. However, if you need a stepping stone, then this is a good product to look at.
text_fidelity_b: Ab Rocket Twister Abdominal Trainer, Red

text_fidelity_a:
Flash Personal Cooking System An absolutely awesome cooking system. Fast, fast, fast! Our initial use for the system will be to boil water for single serve instant coffee packets and to re-hydrate freeze dried food which will keep us and perhaps others happy while camping with the scouts.

Here's a common sense but helpful hint for someone using the Jetboil system for the first time - a no-brainer for anyone who has already cooked with this system:

- If you're just boiling water to pour into another vessel or coffee cup for example, go ahead and fully snap the lid on before beginning your boil. You can conveniently pour through the sipping hole.
- If you're boiling water for the purpose of adding food to the pot such as ramen for example, either lay the lid loosely on top or leave it off altogether.

Why? Because once you snap the lid all the way on and the contents come to a boil you'll burn your fingers trying to get it off unless you use a hot pad or other insulating material.

Highly recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Flash Personal Cooking System

Kubb Yard Game Set by Rally and Roar for Adults, Families - Fun, Interactive Outdoor Family Games - Durable Blocks with Travel Bag - Games for Outside, Lawn, Backyards I had never heard of this game before, but saw this on Amazon and thought it would be a fun thing to take to our next family reunion. It comes in a very nice bag to store everything in as well as take it to parties and gatherings. The instructions are okay, but they were not perfectly clear to me - I couldn't figure out if only the very first team uses the batons or if they switch back and forth like in horseshoes. So I did some googling and found some instructions that are more detailed. I cannot post the link here, but it was simple enough to find with a search - look for the Rules of Kubb poster. I had no idea that this game is such a big deal - there are tournaments for it even! (of course there are :) ).

The kubbs, stakes, and batons are all very well made and I would imagine will hold up well for some time. We've only played a few practice games with my small family but this summer I expect this will be a hit at our huge family reunion. I can't wait to get everyone together to play! It's pretty much its own game, but if I had to compare it to something I'd say if you like horseshoes, bocce ball, curling, bowling, or shuffle board, you'll like this game. Fun for the whole family!

The rest of the kit is pretty nice as well. The little case pouch is handy and compact and has a pocket inside so you can carry a second (and maybe a third) snake in the pouch.

The can of solvent is a little small. It won't last very long if you have multiple guns and go shooting often. But the gun oil should last you a good while.

I liked the bore snake so much I bought one separately (without the kit) for 9mm and one for .22. The .22 bore snake is a bit of a disappointment because it actually doesn't fit down the barrel very easily -- the pull string is almost the same diameter as the barrel itself.

But the .45 bore snake is excellent and so easy.

text_fidelity_a:
Lyweem Cooler Backpack Insulated Leak Proof 38 Cans Lightweight Lunch Backpack Cooler for Men Women Small Soft Cooler Bag According to NPR news I read, Carhartt was forcing it's employees to take an injection if they wanted to remain employed.
I, for one, have a mom who has allergic reactions to most medications and completely understand why some people would fear taking a jab. Because of this, I wanted to keep my support away from Carhartt. Plus, it didn't hurt saving myself $35+ at the time of writing this. I was actually about to buy everything Carhartt I could find that I needed since I've been buying a lot of supplies for work but, hey, I have found some great stuff from these "little guy sellers" and this bag is top notch.

This bag caught my attention because of it's obvious similarity to the Carhartt bag. I received the bag within one day of ordering and the bag looks very well made. No smell as some people complain of smell with products, mine was super clean and well cared for packaging. I wouldn't be surprised if the two brands' bags were made in the same factory - pretty sure both say country of origin is China.

Quality of this Lyweem bag and its zippers appear will be durable. It is comfortable to wear on my shoulders thanks to its padded wide shoulder straps; they don't get all twisted when I put it on like my old bag did - something so annoying I almost never put the old bag on but with this bag no problem.

However, the bag is not completely perfect, at least, perfectly suited for me. Things you may want to consider:
First off, the phone holder is too small for my cell phone. I suspect it would maybe hold phones with up to a 6" screen that are in a case and still be able to zip because mine is very close to fitting snug but nowhere near to zipping but with the case on it's just short of fitting all the way in. My phone is 6.6". (Moto G Power).
Second, I work a job where I have to work out in the rain sometimes and I needed the bag to hold a FROGG TOGGS Men's Classic All-Sport Waterproof Breathable Rain Suit that I also bought from Amazon (the one with the blue jacket is currently only $26). It will fit but it's very tight fit. I thought the bag would be a bit roomier than it actually is. But I also have on top of the suit: 2 pairs of gloves, toothpaste, toothbrush, toboggan, a cloth mask, eye wear, 2 drinks in the side, ibuprofen and sinus medicine, work hat, spare pen and paper with my lunch occupying the bottom.
Third, the bottom section is quite small. I got about 2 2"tall bowls in the bottom. One about 2x6x6 on top of one about 2x8x6. Nothing else but the silverware will fit in the bottom. Can't fit ice packs in with these two sandwich lock n' lock bowls. And with all this said, this is a pretty big bag, honestly. It just takes me more room than I expected.
Fourth, like others have said the bottom section is very awkward how it unfolds but so is the top section (compared to what I am used to). Definitely be aware of this. I am not a fan of how the bag unzips in half at the top. I've only used it once, though, so I might get better used to it. But it zips in half and is just hard to get stuff into it without having to hold it in while I zip it back up. And the bottom unzips and the whole top end just falls back or the bottom falls down. I am sure the Carhartt is just as awkward. So while I am sure they are both great bags, I am not truly a fan of the design as much as I thought I would be. Maybe it'll grow on me? Compared to my other regular backpack this one is tougher to pack.

Lastly, if I had it to do over again for my personal needs, which is a lot of space to carry a lot of stuff - an absurdly lot of stuff I will admit, I would skip this bag and get the Lyweem Duffel bag that also works as a backpack. I think it is $27 and looks like it has a ton more storage space. I would probably get a separate cooler to keep my water and ice packs in. I was thinking about doing this before I bought the bag but I was hoping I wouldn't have to carry 2 bags. I believe I will end up having to get another bag anyway.

At the time of writing this, if Lyweem will continue to make quality products as they have here, this company should go far and last a long time. I will search Lyweem for other needs and support the company as they have supported me with great value. GREAT QUALITY FOR A GREAT PRICE!! DESPITE MY NITPICKS, THIS PRODUCT IS A WINNER!!
text_fidelity_b: Lyweem Cooler Backpack Insulated Leak Proof 38 Cans Lightweight Lunch Backpack Cooler for Men Women Small Soft Cooler Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Klymit Insulated Static V Luxe Inflatable Sleeping Pad for Camping, Lightweight Hiking and Backpacking Air Bed For Cold Weather, 3 Inch Thick I've previously owned a Klymit V without the "Luxe," but a piece of the one valve it had broke off in short order. This Klymit V Luxe has valves which *appear* to me to have fewer fiddly parts, and there are two of them--more on why that's good in a moment!

First off, these pads have a smart design. Although there is no railing per say, the Vs help to keep you on them which is good news if you do not stay in one place on a bed. The material keeps the air inside from feeling cold (and presumably from drinking in too much of the earth's cold).

The primary use I gave my original V was as a buffer between me and an extremely ill-suited new mattress while I desperately shopped for solutions. And although I've been a backpacker in the past, sadly, my primary intended use for the Static V Luxe is to act as a buffering layer when I need to sleep on other people's mattresses. I have considerable back health issues, and this padding is incredibly helpful for when I cannot be on my own mattress. I purchased this size this time because the original V is so much smaller than a twin bed that it was downright silly trying to use it for my purpose. Also I use a body pillow and change positions a lot. This will clearly be nicer for managing nights out of my own bed.

Now I saw someone complaining about the two valves because they are confusing. This person has probably never experienced the downsides of only having one valve for letting air out of a mattress. Sure, you need to be certain that the valve you are not blowing into is closed so that the mattress can properly inflate, but oh, my word, it is soooooo much easier to get the air out of this mattress pad! I could almost never get my original V small enough to properly stick into its dry sack. But this larger V luxe easily packs up smaller than I could get the original V to go. Ok, so maybe "easy" is relative. You do need to open both valves, roll it down from bottom to top, open it up again, fold a few times, and roll once more to get it maximally small. But it actually works and stuffs in the drysack.

I hope if you're reading this that you have more adventurous uses afoot, but I do recommend this Static V Luxe and wish I'd had one back when I was a backpacker!
text_fidelity_b: Klymit Insulated Static V Luxe Inflatable Sleeping Pad for Camping, Lightweight Hiking and Backpacking Air Bed For Cold Weather, 3 Inch Thick

The hammock took longer than expected to arrive - but not to worry-- we patiently checked Amazon tracking on a daily basis to see when the refreshment of lying on a soft, sturdy hammock whilst sipping a cocktail - would arrive at our door. After waiting on the edge of our plastic lawn chairs for two weeks, the big day finally arrived! The hammock was delivered by our friendly Amazon courier and shouts of joy could be heart resounding through the halls of our home! Two of our sons ceremoniously carried the long hammock box into the house like a wealthy Roman patron being carried through the streets on a litter. The box was opened and said hammock was unrolled like a precious scroll. Visions of hours spent snoozing under a canopy of trees danced in the heads of family members as they clamored to put this 'Object of 'Liesure and Rest' onto the stand that had carried our old, canvas, LL BEAN hammock. After 14 years of service, that good sanctuary had finally rotted away. (Actually, I wasn't home for this part, but I'm sure this is how it went.)

Our faithful and strong sons set the hammock up beneath towering Tulip Populars, wafting in the refreshing breeze and waited for me to come home hoping to unveil a pleasant surprise for the beloved mother. I arrived home, hot, sweaty and tired from a long day of horseback riding with my faithful steed. A persistent headache was pounding in my brain from hours of tracking desperados through the forests. (Ok, I was actually trying to catch up to my friends who had galloped away rather prematurely.) Anyway, as I slogged through the house, wilted and exhausted, my god-like son winked at me whilst ushering me through the back door to the paradise that awaited in the back yard.

THERE IT WAS! THE HAMMOCK for which I had been longing! I sat down on the side and stretched my battered frame onto the hammock like Cleopatra reclining under a gold-embroidered canopy dressed as Aphrodite, (but wearing riding boots and half-chaps).....only to discover that the hammock of my dreams was an imposter!!!! THIS WAS NO SOFT BED OF ROSES TO LIE ON! NO! IT FELT LIKE BAD CARPET ON THE WALLS OF A CHEAP MOTEL! I stifled my revulsion and tried to get comfortable but it was no use. The fabric wasn't fabric at all - it felt like plastic water bottles woven into a nightmarish tapestry by well-intentioned environmentalists! I leapt from this bed of vipers disgusted and disappointed. My family pleaded with me to give it another chance, saying "It's not so bad, we like it!" "Philistines!!!!" I retorted! " THIS. WILL. NOT. DO!" whilst gnashing my teeth to the best of my ability. To which they shrugged and got the box out of the trash so we could return it.

Postscript - If you want a comfy hammock made out of sunbrella fabric, you have to spend about $250 these days. I found one on Wayfair and now we are anxiously awaiting that one to be delivered. Cheers! :)
text_fidelity_b: ALGOMA 2781SPC Quick Dry Hammock, 13-Feet, Earth Tones

text_fidelity_a:
Razor E300 Electric Scooter - 9" Air-filled Tires, Up to 15 mph and 10 Miles Range, White/Blue I just put some rubber bands on the throttle so it felt grippier. This thing is the most fun! I am 5'10 and weigh 180. It does have a hard time on hills but on flat land and down hill it can feel pretty fast. If you want to ride around town just choose flattest routes.

Like with a skateboard....once you learn the correct foot positions to ride comfortably, it is easy. I learned I put my feet on very similar as to my skateboards.

Since the throttle is either on or off with no inbetween....it can feel kind of jerky the first few times you ride it until you get used to that. You will learn it fast though....how to let off or turn on. Turning is not very tight radius so practice that if you arent used to riding one.
Prices are wild on these. I got mine last month for 260...the white e300 with the blue front forks. I see they are over 400 now. I think under 275 is a solid price if you want to play or plan to ride it to your local store or other near by places. Scooter laws vary state to state and where I am this is considered a toy and can be ridden on the sidewalks. Which....no one ever uses here anyway. We dont have bike lanes where I live either so I dont know if it would be legal to ride a bike lane in my state.

It is beefy and heavy and feels like a true machine rather than a toy. Mine charges fine, tires hold pressure fine, no issues at all.
I keep it inside because it flat states on the directions of use that extreme temps can effect the battery or even ruin it.
I have used it on street pavement, sidewalks, and fine gravel. I have never run out of charge on a trip but you CAN still kick scoot this old style if you do run out of charge.

I think it is fun, gets me out in the fresh air, saves some gas money.
text_fidelity_b: Razor E300 Electric Scooter - 9" Air-filled Tires, Up to 15 mph and 10 Miles Range, White/Blue

I do believe the best flash killers are the ones that thread directly inside of the objective lenses that have internal threads.  Those options are also a lot more money. Kowela ab Trainer Ab Roller Wheel for Abdominal Muscle Training, Abdominal Exercise Equipment, Perfect Abdominal core Carver Fitness Workout for Abdominal Muscles There are many positive Amazon reviews on this ab roller. And there are definitely some good points for sure.

The wheel is WIDE. So it's very stable during movements. The width also allows easy turns. So you can create a variety of angles for your ab workouts. It also has a spring mechanism that prevents the roller from over-extending. Therefore keeps you from hyper-extending! Or at least that's the concept.

However, my main concern, is with the construction.

It's made entirely of plastic (namely the handles) with a thin tread of rubber to act as the gripping portion of the wheel. Although there is a "metal" rod that acts as the axle, I'm not sure if it's steel. And during use, you are exerting A LOT of force on these plastic handles. And while it appears that they are sturdy, something feels just a little questionable. The rolling mechanism is not smooth. As if the handles may give out mid-exercise.

I would have preferred steel & rubber for the axle/handle assembly. It would have just felt more durable/comfortable. And I'm not sure if there are any bearings, but this would have at least taken the friction off of the axle. As it appears to be rolling directly against the plastic of the wheel. Of course, this unit is under $30.00. So possibly that's not to be expected at this price point.

However, you don't want your mind focused on the quality of your exercise equipment while your working out. So if that's at all a concern for you, possible consider a higher end ab roller (if such a thing exists!).

Osprey Packs Pandion Daypack The Osprey Pandion Daypack (OPD) is the best backpack I've ever had. No detail has been overlooked. It has everything. I'm still discovering features I didn't notice over the first few days.

I use my backpack for four things - schlepping my documents and portable office supplies for work back and forth to the office, for carrying my portable electronic supplies, for clothes/toiletries etc. for short airplane trips, and for long day hikes. I did all of this and more last weekend when I traveled to New Hampshire for three days which included a four mile hike, and two days when I needed to check in at work using my laptop.

There are three main compartments, each of which has its own partitions, sleeves, a lanyard, and in one of them, a waterproof lining. The pack itself has a stiff outer frame that comes in hand for a long hike, makes it easier to stand the pack up on its own, and allows for pack to be flattened out for light cargo, or fully expanded for air travel or a large payload. There are multiple exterior sleeves for water bottles, papers, and other items that are convenient to have quick at hand. Each zipper features a plastic loop which makes them easier to grab and pull.

The pack has multiple pull tight straps in a variety of places, including waist and chest straps that makes it easier to carry heavier weight, or using the straps on the outside, compress it down for lighter trips back and forth to the office. Its got a stout handle at the top. Taught mesh fabric has been stretched between the frame in the back, which provides good comfort for toting heavier weight, and allowing air to get in behind your back as you are moving along.

It's good looking, light, and it comes with a lifetime guarantee. Please peruse the multiple photos I took of the pack a few days ago (as usual, having difficulty with Amazon photo upload functionality. I'll add photos after balance of review posts.) This is a very impressive daypack from all standpoints including function, appearance, features, and weight.
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Packs Pandion Daypack

Saris Bones Car Bike Rack, Trunk or Hitch Carrier, Mount 2-4 Bicycles It takes about 5 minutes to adjust the straps. The Saris Bones 3 fits easily on my 2009 Chevy Malibu and my son's SUV. I suggest that you watch the videos showing how to put it on your vehicle. The Saris customer service is very good if you have any questions.

My Trek hybrid sits securely in the smartly shaped bike cradles, and the cradle straps and seat tube anti-sway strap keep it steady even when traveling down the freeway. I've only used it to carry two bikes, but like the ability to carry a third bike. It's nice to be able to pull directly into my garage after returning from a cycling trip.

The soft rubber feet on the four arms haven't scuffed the finish on the vehicles, and the hot Texas sun hasn't caused the strap clips or rubber feet to discolor the clear coat. You should always wipe clean the car trunk and bottom of the rubber feet before putting on the rack.

I chose the Saris Bones 3 after talking with other cyclist and reading the reviews. I'm glad I bought it, and understand why it's been popular for so many years.

text_fidelity_a:
Moxi Skates - Beach Bunny - Fashionable Womens Roller Skates Color: Watermelon. Skate Size: 7 (My normal shoe/boot size is 8-8.5 in US womens)
First, they are soooo cute! I love the color combo. I'm 50 yrs old and decided to get back into roller skating. I used to do this casually when I was in my teens, but was never exceptional at it. I thought this would be a fun way to get some more exercise in my life. So far its working! You engage so many muscles when roller skating. It takes balance, core and leg strength to keep from falling on your bum. These are made of vinyl so they are quite stiff at first and take some time break in. My hubby purchased these as a gift. He purchased according to the size chart and they fit well/snug with a thick sock. I normally wear a size 8 in U.S women’s shoes. When it comes to boots I typically buy 8.5 (to allow for thicker sock). Hubby purchased the size 7 skates as the chart indicated. This was just right. I thought they might be a bit tight at first. But with use, I realized the size was perfect. You want your foot to be held firmly as you will be moving around a lot. I imagine if they were looser, my foot would flex more and potentially cause strain in the foot muscles so I think the snug sizing is perfect. Measure your foot and look at size chart and you should be fine. I like that the skates have a metal base plate instead of plastic. This feels sturdier/safer. The wheels roll well on blacktop streets (even better on my hardwood floors inside my house). There are a couple things that were a bit odd. First the vinyl is so thick its a bit uncomfortable (specifically around the ankle) until they get worn in. And it takes a while to wear them in.
Second, the laces on one skate were a whole foot longer than the laces on the other skate. This trips out my OCD brain. I will have to replace them.

Overall, I think these are good skates for beginners (of all ages). They are made well and of good quality. Just be patient with the wear in period.
text_fidelity_b: Moxi Skates - Beach Bunny - Fashionable Womens Roller Skates

text_fidelity_a:
Plano Stowaway Micro Organizer Premium Tackle Organization I don't know why everybody is having problems with these 3214 boxes. I've been using them for years - at least 10 years - the brownish kind that's labeled "Micro Mag". I've never had a single problem with them and I prefer them over the 3414 soft plastic white ones, although these are slightly heavier than the 3414's. When I want to just carry one little kit in my vest or pocket, these are perfect. I've accidentally dropped them on hard surfaces without any breakage or cracks. Of course, I'm sure there's a limit to how much abuse they will take, but if you're careful with your fishing gear there should be no problem.

Since I gave two of them away to my son and wife, I needed a replacement. I tried to consolidate all of my trout gear into one, but found I could be a little more organized with two. I use one for all my terminal tackle, hooks and weights (separated by size) and I'll use the other one for all my lures. The problem I have with the white 3414 box is that the lids don't seal tightly. Every one I've ever had or inspected on the shelf has the same issue. The lids are slightly bowed out. So, when you put a bunch of tiny #14 hooks, swivels, and the like, they always end up migrating to another section. Really irritating. That NEVER happens with the hard 3214.

When I saw these green ones (I've never seen them in the stores), I thought it was perfect. I like the color and it differentiates between my brown one. Comparing it to my old brown one, it is exactly the same - except mine is not labeled Micro Mag like in the picture. The top is just kind of plain with a small Plano logo. I actually prefer this because it makes seeing the contents easier.

As far as all the complaints with the latches not catching, I have NO idea what that's all about. I've handled dozens of these things and never seen that problem, nor have I ever gotten one that didn't work perfectly. You'd have to have pretty poor quality control to let so many go out into the market as seem to be reported, and I personally think Plano has pretty good QC.
text_fidelity_b: Plano Stowaway Micro Organizer Premium Tackle Organization

text_fidelity_a: Hunting: Edge By Expedite H2o Quiver Magnet There is a little lever that rotates over the batteries, so they don't fall out. therefore batteries falling out is not an issue. I cut a small piece of  Remington camo cloth for the top of the lids to knock off the glare and place two or three of these among 6 decoys in several spots around the blind.  They give lots of movement to the decoys and they really draw the ducks on calm days.  Battery life is not very good, so you will need to change them daily if you spend more than four or five hours in the blind and I find that if I replace the batteries at the end of the hunt if needed it just takes a moment to set them out for the next hunt.  I can't imagine a cheaper easier way to put some movement in your spread and will always use them.  I buy the 100 box of AA batteries as that is the most economical purchase.  Don't buy the bargain batteries, just use copper top as they last the longest.

text_fidelity_a: SUNLITE Unicycle Cotterless Steel Crank Arm Set, Silver The first unicycle I had was in Germany when I was with the US Army in Heidelberg. It was a VERY hard to ride 26 or 28 inch. Not a good one to learn on. Changing it to a 24 inch by rebuilding the wheel (but keeping the same long cranks) made it much easier to ride. That was in 1983 and that unicycle has since worn out. (I rode it a LOT, all over the World!) But newer unicycles lacked the same quality of that ride and the "feel" was all wrong. I didn't even know that cranks came in different lengths in 1983, but reducing the large wheel diameter while keeping the 6 inch cranks is what made the ride so nice. (With shorter cranks it's not as easy to balance or pedal, and you go too fast- not impossible but not as much fun.) Proof of that came with these 6 inch SUNLITE cotterless cranks which changed the performance of a 24 inch that came with 5 inch cranks to finding that "sweet spot" it had been missing. They're very heavy and strong, I doubt I'll be able to bend these.
text_fidelity_b: SUNLITE Unicycle Cotterless Steel Crank Arm Set, Silver
